acceptanceCriteria: unplannedread.Read and observations.Read apply the writer's row contract on read (kind, tool or code membership, project-relative path, non-negative bytes) and count each rejected row by a closed reason instead of skipping silently.
Both readers report when the file exceeded maxFileBytes and was cut, and slotlearn.ReadLabels surfaces that alongside Truncated.
slotlearn.ReadLabels excludes empty and non-project-relative paths; a regression test feeds {}, an escaping path, a negative byte count and an unknown kind and shows none becomes a label.
body: Filed 2026-10-04 from the V1-0712 output-class inventory (docs/build-log/2026-10-04-v1-0712-output-class-inventory.md), source origin/main a2615609. Confirmed from source, runtime NOT_RUN. The writers of the two private ledgers enforce closed contracts (unplannedread HookPostToolSession: closed tool set and projectpath containment; observations Append/validateWriterContract: closed kinds, codes and validObservationPath). The readers do not re-apply them. unplannedread foldRow (unplannedread.go:804) skips non-JSON rows without counting them and treats any row with an empty kind as an unplanned read, so {} adds an empty path and {"path":"../../x","bytes":-5} adds an escaping path with negative bytes. observations readRow (observations.go readRow) re-validates only proof and adapter-degradation rows; a hand- or agent-written file-change event with touchedPaths ["../../x"] becomes a Miss, and rows failing strictJSONObject or renderedKeysLineSafe are dropped uncounted. Both read through io.LimitReader(maxFileBytes+1) (128 KiB) and do not report that an over-cap file was cut. slotlearn ReadLabels (slotlearn.go:50) unions both outputs into labels without re-validation, and ServingSlot defaults unknown or empty paths to the definition class. The held-out gate (LTA-V0-009..012) still decides admission, so poisoned labels can steer which proposals are scored but cannot bypass the gate. Invariant 4 says the ledgers are inputs to learning only through this step, so the step should admit only rows the writer could have produced.
title: Ledger readers admit rows the writer refuses, and those rows become slot-learning labels
